title: Hard questions, three months in
hook: The questions that come at month three are sharper. That's not a bad sign. It means you're taking this seriously.

screens.text: In the first weeks, doubts were often vague: "Did I do the right thing?" Three months in, they get specific: one verse, one rule, one thing about men and women that won't sit right. On Day 33 you learned first aid for doubts. Today: how to work a hard question through.

**You're asking what most converts ask.** In a survey of 618 American converts, the top two sources of doubt were rules about men and women (44%) and feeling that the rules limit freedom (37%) [Yaqeen 2025].
bubbles: So if this is where your mind goes, you're not broken and you're not alone.
These questions have been asked, and answered by serious scholars, for centuries.

screens.text: Drag along the line. A hard question is a dip you work through, not the end of the road.

screens.title: Six moves for a hard question

steps.text: **Name it.** Write the exact question in one sentence. Vague worries feel huge; named ones shrink.
**Check the source.** Find what the verse or hadith actually says, with its context, not a clip.
**Ask a teacher.** A qualified teacher can show you how scholars have understood it for centuries.
**Separate Islam from Muslims.** Some Muslims' behavior isn't the teaching itself.
**Weigh it.** Set it next to everything else you know is true about Allah and His Messenger ﷺ.
**Keep praying.** Hold the question while you keep praying and making du'a. You don't have to pause your faith to think.

screens.done_text: Name it, check it, ask, separate, weigh, and keep praying.

screens.text: **On men and women, start with what's fixed.** The Qur'an promises a good life and full reward to whoever does good, *"whether male or female"* [Q 16:97, Saheeh Intl.].
bubbles: Allah says He won't let the work of any worker be lost, man or woman [Q 3:195]. He lists believing women beside believing men again and again [Q 33:35].
Some rulings do differ, like dress and some family roles. Different isn't the same as worth less.

screens.prompt: Build the Qur'an's promise [Q 16:97]: whoever does good…
screens.answer: gets a good life and full reward, male or female
screens.feedback: Same promise, same reward. No one's good work is lost, man or woman [Q 3:195].

screens.text: **On freedom, ask "free from what?"** Everyone serves something: money, approval, cravings, a phone. Islam's claim is that serving the One who made you frees you from being owned by all of that [Yaqeen, *Honored Since Adam*].
bubbles: And your faith itself is free: *"There shall be no compulsion in [acceptance of] the religion"* [Q 2:256, Saheeh Intl.].
Most of life is halal. The limits are few.

screens.title: Thoughts that show up with a hard question

cards.front: "If I can't explain this rule, my faith must be fake."
cards.back: No. You trust many things you can't fully explain. Faith rests on what you do know: Allah, the Qur'an, the Prophet ﷺ. One open question doesn't erase that.

cards.front: "Struggling with a rule means I've rejected it."
cards.back: No. Feeling unsure is not leaving Islam. Leaving is a choice to reject it. Struggling while you keep praying is what believers do.

cards.front: "I should hide this from everyone at the masjid."
cards.back: Hidden questions grow. A good teacher has heard yours before and won't be shocked.{women} You can ask for a female mentor.{/women}
Some answers take weeks of learning. Allah doesn't burden anyone beyond what they can bear [Q 2:286]. You can hold a question and still live your faith.

chips: Why don't men and women inherit the same?
Why do women cover and men don't?
Can women be scholars and leaders in Islam?
If Allah gave us free will, why so many rules?
I want to talk to a woman about this

screens.prompt: Write down the one question that's been sitting with you, in a single sentence. Then write one thing you're still sure of. You can share both with your mentor.

screens.text: **When to call in a person.** The AI guide can explain and point you to sources, but some questions need a human who knows you. Bring yours to {{mentor.name}} or your imam, or use "Ask my imam" anonymously.
bubbles: If a doubt comes with constant anxiety, sleepless nights or dark thoughts, tell someone soon. That deserves care, not just answers.

screens.text: Send your one-sentence question somewhere real today.
steps: Take the question you just wrote
Send it to {{mentor.name}}, to your imam with "Ask my imam" (it can be anonymous), or to the AI guide to start
screens.optional_extra: Then do one thing that feeds your faith: pray on time, read a page of the Qur'an, or sit with Muslim friends.

screens.text: Name the question, check the source, ask a real teacher, and keep praying while you look. A question is not a rejection.
Asking hard questions is part of a grown-up faith. You're doing it well.

check.prompt: What does the Qur'an say about the reward of men and women who do good?

options.text: Both get a good life and full reward
options.feedback: Right [Q 16:97]. No one's good work is lost, man or woman [Q 3:195].

options.text: Only men's deeds are fully rewarded
options.feedback: Not quite. The Qur'an promises the same reward to whoever does good, male or female [Q 16:97].

check.prompt: You have a doubt you can't answer yet. What's true?

options.text: Feeling unsure isn't leaving Islam; keep praying and ask a teacher
options.feedback: Right. Leaving is a choice to reject Islam. A question is something you work through.

options.text: You should stop praying until you're sure
options.feedback: Not quite. Keep praying while you look. Prayer is where you ask Allah for clarity.

aiContext:
**Lesson facts**
- Yaqeen *Becoming Muslim* (2025; n=618 US converts): 23% said doubts made them consider leaving; top doubt topics were gender rules (44%), rules restricting freedom (37%) and intolerance of Muslims (37%); God's existence 21%. Doubt is linked to anxiety and intolerance of uncertainty; doubts usually ease with time, Muslim friends and a capable imam [Yaqeen 2025; Research Notes - Retention and Convert Voices R1].
- Equal reward and worth: [Q 16:97], [Q 3:195], [Q 33:35]. Some rulings differ by gender.
- Freedom: Islam frames worship of Allah as freedom from servitude to desires and created things; human dignity and moral choice are honored [Yaqeen, *Honored Since Adam*]. No compulsion in religion [Q 2:256].
- Feeling unsure is not leaving Islam; leaving is a choice to reject it (scholar question Q20). Distress over doubts can itself be a sign of faith [Muslim 132].
- Day 33 covered first aid (doubts are normal, write it down, whispers vs. questions). This lesson is a method for a specific question; don't repeat Day 33.

**Likely questions** (Spec §6.2 rule 5: take doubts seriously; never shame, never pressure; never argue anyone into belief; offer a mentor or scholar)
- *"Why don't men and women inherit the same?"* Brief, mainstream: in some cases a son inherits double a daughter's share; classical scholars connect this to the man's sole legal duty to provide for wife and family, while a woman's wealth, including her mahr [Q 4:4], is hers alone. In other cases shares are equal (for example, a deceased person's mother and father with children). Offer the imam for details; don't calculate shares for real estates (legal advice).
- *"Why do women cover and men don't?"* Both are commanded to be modest and lower their gaze [Q 24:30–31]; dress rules differ. Day 38 and 59 covered this. Offer a female mentor.
- *"Can women be scholars?"* Yes: many of the greatest early transmitters of hadith were women, starting with Aisha. Stay general; don't invent names or numbers.
- *"Why so many rules if we have free will?"* Most things are allowed (Day 49); limits protect people; choosing to obey is itself the use of free will. Ask which rule weighs most, and route specifics.
- *"I want to talk to a woman."* Offer the female mentor or staff path (rule 12) and the "Ask my imam" queue.

**Escalate:** any doubt the convert wants a human for; personal rulings (marriage, divorce, inheritance in their own family); questions on apostasy, slavery, or specific penalties (fixed-topic, rule 11); signs of distress (safety rule 6).

**Don't**
- Don't dismiss or rush the feeling, and don't claim every hard question has a two-line answer.
- Don't say "that rule is just cultural" when it's a real ruling; separate culture from religion honestly.
- Don't debate; explain, then offer a person.
